headline: Plan-fix-verify loop runs until tests pass — uncapped iteration creates cascading-error risk if the critic misjudges.
name: Plan → Fix → Verify Loop

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Inputs to the loop are internal (bug reports, test output) and not user-controlled; injection risk is minimal unless test output contains adversarial data.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Loop operates within a single codebase; data leakage only occurs if test fixtures or logs expose secrets.

conditions: planner and executor use different versions of code
mitigations: share repo snapshot between planner and executor
C_capability_conflict.rationale: Planner and executor both use claude-code in different roles (planning vs patching), creating risk of conflicting assumptions if the planner's bug diagnosis does not match the executor's fix.

D_cascading_error.rationale: If the test-runner critic incorrectly marks a broken fix as passing, the loop continues with corrupted state. Without a hard iteration limit or external validation, this can cascade indefinitely.

E_compliance.rationale: Loop is confined to code-level debugging; no regulated data is inherently processed unless the codebase itself contains compliance logic.
